method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a seat-neutral core (voca-core.l4, six regulative rules), the Motor Accident Insurance Act 1994 s 37(2)-(3) brought in narrowly (voca-mai-s37.l4, one regulative rule), date helpers (voca-dates.l4) and a seat layer (voca-seat.l4) that restates no rule; no REFUSE (an act of violence before 2 September 2024 answers `not covered`, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Victims of Crime Assistance Act 2009 (Qld) (act-2009-035), the version in force from 2 September 2024 (current on 20 October 2026), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2009-035.txt; with the Motor Accident Insurance Act 1994 (Qld) (act-1994-009), current in-force version on 22 September 2026, s 37(2)-(3) and the s 4 definition of motor vehicle accident only, as deposited at ../../../motor-accident-insurance-act-1994/registers/source-bundle/act-1994-009.txt. All amounts are in the Act and Schedule 2; no regulation under the Act is in force.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run voca-dates.l4 ; l4 run voca-mai-s37.l4 ; l4 run voca-core.l4 ; l4 run voca-seat.l4 ; l4 run voca-cases-applicant.l4
checks.result: 183 assertions satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-10-24); 7 #TRACEs with an expect line (6 breaches, 1 refund still owed), each read and as expected
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: From the seat of the applicant: s 5; ss 21, 23, 24; ss 25, 25A, 25B (series as a fact); s 26; s 27; s 28 (as a fact); Part 3 ss 31-34 (workers' compensation, its facts as inputs); Part 3A ss 36A-36F with MAI Act s 37(2)-(3) and s 4 (motor vehicle accident); Part 3B ss 36G-36J (NIISQ facts as inputs); Parts 4-8 ss 37-50; Schedule 2 (special assistance, categories A-D and category A-C circumstances); ss 51, 52, 54-61; ss 78-82 with s 21(2)-(3); s 85 (input percentage); s 86 and the Schedule 3 definition of relevant payment; ss 89(2), 98(2), 141A, 141B; ss 97-100; s 101; s 106G; s 123; s 126; ss 124-125. Out: Part 16 (recovery from the offender), Part 12 information-gathering powers and other deferrals (ss 62-77, 83-84C, 87), ss 88-96 except s 89(2), the rest of Parts 15 and 17, administration (Parts 19-20, chapters 2, 4, 5 except ss 141A-141B), transitional chapters 6-11, and acts of violence before 2 September 2024. Read with subjects/au/social-security-act-1991/ (s 17(2B): criminal injury compensation is not compensation), subjects/au/income-tax-assessment-act-1997/ (s 118-37) and subjects/au/qld/workers-compensation-and-rehabilitation-act-2003/; cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seat: the applicant for assistance (primary, parent secondary, witness secondary or related victim, or the person applying for funeral expense assistance)
